{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZc3R0A", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhDEE30", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 89, "title": "Add conservative sender-visible read confirmation for local resident mail", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `c439d6dea21a1e2ac93c391109c99589bd0ed03d`, a human can send a letter and receive a resident reply, but cannot inspect recipient-read confirmation:

- `src/mail.ts:renderMailList` displays read state only for INBOX; SENT has no recipient status.
- `renderMail` displays no read confirmation.
- `src/storage/schema.ts:validateMailRelations` permits `readAt` only for human recipients.
- `src/storage/repository.ts:commitAiRun` transactionally saves resident replies without recording confirmation for their explicit parent.

This leaves the send → check sent mail → receive reply journey incomplete relative to documented PC-VAN capabilities. It is an existing fidelity gap, not a demonstrated regression from PR #88.

## Expected outcome

A human can inspect SENT and READ before and after an authorized resident reply commits. Before confirmation, status means **unknown/unconfirmed**, never proven unread. After commitment, only the explicit parent letter shows a durable recipient-read confirmation and its projected historical time.

Use successful resident reply commitment as a conservative fictional confirmation event. Preserve ordinary human-recipient read marking and all existing mail routes, scheduling, consent and privacy boundaries.

## Context

### Historical evidence and reconstruction

Sources inspected live on 2026-10-24:

- An NEC PC-VAN office account in March 1993, printed page 231, explicitly describes checking when the recipient read sent mail. Confidence is high for the documented earlier capability; continuity into late 1996 is a moderate-confidence assumption. Its earlier retention policy must not become a target-year requirement. [NEC account](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jkg/43/3/43_KJ00002959297/_pdf/-char/ja)
- A Windows 95 client-author description independently lists checking whether sent mail was read. Confidence is high in the stated capability; the release date and target-year applicability remain unresolved. Client automation does not authenticate host commands. [Client description](https://www.vector.co.jp/soft/win95/net/se024554.html)
- November 1996 documentation separately establishes PC-VAN Internet-mail addressing through `INET#` and outbound uuencoding. This local increment must not imply that historical PC-VAN lacked external mail. [Internet Magazine, p. 221](https://iwparchives.jp/wp-content/themes/twentytwelve/bn/pdf/im199611-220-mail2.pdf)

Focused searches for sent-mail checking, read/open confirmation and 1996 controls recovered no qualifying target-year host sequence. CROCUS retrieval failed; its indexed description concerns mail automation, not confirmation syntax. The preserved ECOM page returned 403 and concerns a distinct postal service. Accessible NEC, client-author and contemporary publisher sources supplied alternatives.

**Accepted category D reconstruction:** a newly committed, validated resident reply confirms its explicit parent at commitment. This is a local simulation rule, not a recovered PC-VAN read-event mechanism. Prompt context contains bounded excerpts, so commitment does not demonstrate that a model examined every line. Exact Japanese labels, placement and confirmation timing remain reconstructed. Reading without replying remains unknown; this Issue adds no independent resident-reading scheduler.

### Implementation and history

`validateMailGeneration` already pins the resident, human correspondent and explicit reply parent. `commitAiRun` checks current authorization and performs mail insertion and run completion inside the existing world-fenced transaction. Reuse that boundary and its notification path. `serviceDate` supplies the existing historical-calendar projection.

[Issue #83](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/83) is completed and explicitly excludes sender-read lifecycle. [Issue #52](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/52) established local mail and human read markers. Live repository queries returned no open Issues or PRs; no equivalent pending handoff was found.

[PR #88](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/pull/88) and `docs/validation.md` report 297 passing checks, configured type checking/build and production journeys, with initial failures and their corrections disclosed. These are Coordinator records; this research graph did not rerun them.

Scope excludes mailbox migration, Internet-mail delivery, binary mail, new historical commands, retention changes and inference-driven reading without replies.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Show concise recipient-confirmation status in human SENT rows and sent-letter READ output through MAIN `1`, MAIN `X` and SIG `MAIL`. Unconfirmed output must clearly mean unknown, using wording such as `確認なし`; do not label it `未読`. Confirmed details expose the confirmation time. Preserve existing identity/name presentation, mailbox selection and return contexts.
- [ ] Record confirmation only when a **new** authorized resident reply successfully commits, and only on `run.mail.replyToMailId`. Save the parent confirmation, new reply, number allocation and run completion atomically. Planning, prompt construction, incidental context inclusion, public followups, resident initiation and rendering create no confirmation.
- [ ] Use narrowly scoped optional metadata with explicit reconstruction provenance and association to the confirming reply, or an equivalently strict representation. Validate timestamps and same-correspondent reply relationships on writes and imports; reject malformed, dangling or mismatched confirmation evidence. Preserve current human-recipient `readAt` semantics and restrictions. Maintain relationship-safe deletion behavior for any new persisted references.
- [ ] Preserve the first recorded confirmation instant. Use an operational commitment time no earlier than the parent creation time, documenting any clock clamp. Render it through the existing calendar without storing projected 1996 strings. Catch-up `simulatedAt`, reload time and later retries must not replace the confirmation time.
- [ ] Invalid output, failed generation, cancellation, consent withdrawal, resident pause, stale-world work and transaction/quota failure create no new confirmation. Duplicate-run and duplicate-parent suppression must not invent or refresh confirmation. A signal abort before transaction completion rolls back both reply and confirmation.
- [ ] Accept existing databases and backups with no confirmation metadata, including older reply pairs, without backfilling inferred events. Export/import preserves newly recorded evidence and exact operational timestamps. Invalid imports leave the original world intact; reset removes confirmations with mail. Restored or reset worlds retain existing cross-tab and in-flight generation fences.
- [ ] Extend existing Playwright coverage in `tests/mail-repository.spec.ts`, `tests/mail-autonomy.spec.ts`, `tests/mail.spec.ts` and presentation coverage as appropriate. Cover the selected parent versus another context letter, initiation without confirmation, immutable timestamps, concurrent/idempotent commitment, duplicate-parent suppression, invalid routing/output, consent/pause/cancellation, rollback after confirmation has been attempted, old-backup compatibility, invalid-import atomicity, reload/restore and reset/stale work. Use controlled clocks and existing mocked inference.
- [ ] Include a production keyboard journey: WRITE → review/send → SENT/READ unconfirmed → mocked authorized resident reply commitment → SENT/READ confirmed → reload and backup/restore. Exercise all three mail entry routes. Confirm human INBOX marking remains individual and unchanged, and that background activity preserves an active draft and IME composition. Existing notification refresh must not overwrite terminal input.
- [ ] Preserve literal Japanese subjects/bodies, numbering, reply links, member IDs, operational creation/simulation dates, private-context bounds, scheduling and save budgets. Protected-record comparisons should allow only the intended parent metadata, new reply, allocation and normal activity bookkeeping. Preserve existing functional, storage, consent, IME, terminal and other-service regression coverage.
- [ ] Update `docs/mail.md`, relevant storage/schema documentation, the historical research record and applicable About descriptions. Record URLs, inspection date, historical scope, confidence and accepted reconstruction; explicitly retain the unknown reading-without-reply case. Keep routine terminal output concise and provenance on existing documentation/About surfaces.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs documented `npm test`; the existing Playwright configuration includes `npm run build`, TypeScript checking and production assets. Record actual outcomes and disclose failures or skipped checks. Review the full diff, affected documentation links and `git diff --check`. Use existing tooling without new frameworks or model downloads.

## Optional validation

A newly recovered dated PC-VAN mail transcript may later refine labels, placement and timing. Additional native-IME or subjective historical-layout comparisons are optional; no human, hardware or real-model check is required for completion.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. All acceptance checks are achievable before merge.
